info.title: Pidgen Public API
info.description: The published subset of the Pidgen App Service HTTP API. Declare the version a client was written against in the PIDGEN-API-Version request header.

delete.description: Remove the Agent's open preference draft and its rows. The published version, if any, is left exactly as it is and keeps applying. The discard is recorded as a command (status applied) and audited. With no open draft the command is refused with disposition_code TEAM_MEMBER_PREFERENCE_DRAFT_NOT_FOUND and a sentence in disposition_detail.message; an expected_version the Agent no longer has is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT. Repeating the request with its idempotency_key answers the first command. Requires agent.manage; an Agent that is not in the Account is 404 AGENT_NOT_FOUND.

get.description: List the tickets that publishing the Agent's preferences now sends back to planning, so a person sees them before confirming: the tickets of the Agent that are ready to start, ordered by Project then id. Publishing withdraws exactly these, so they are planned again with the new preferences; a running ticket keeps the preferences it started with, and a ticket in Backlog or planning uses the new ones when planned, so neither is listed. Reading it changes nothing. Requires agent.manage; an Agent that is not in the Account is 404 AGENT_NOT_FOUND.

get.description: List open review gates, clarifications, planning decisions, recovery, workflow attention and operational findings in the Account named by X-PIDGEN-Account — only its Tickets, and for an Account Member only those of their Projects. Each decision names its target (a step, run, dependency or the Ticket) and carries actions: every action decided for that target, with whether it is allowed, whether you may take it, whether it is recommended, and the typed refusal when it is not allowed. Decisions with a recommended action come first, then the newest. Returns counts for me, claimable, following, all and on_hold. Following returns no findings and lists followed work not waiting on you; other views return an empty following list. on_hold lists the open hold reviews (code hold_review, label Keep holding ‹ticket key›?) in your review_scope, oldest hold first, whoever they are addressed to: the whole Account for an Account Owner or Administrator, the Projects you manage for a Project Manager, nothing for anyone else. Requires ticket.read.

post.summary: Apply a bulk action to previewed Inbox decisions
post.description: Request the action for each previewed item that is still what was previewed. Every item is checked again: one that changed since its preview is excluded with PREVIEW_STALE, one you may not change with FORBIDDEN and one with nothing to change with NO_EFFECT; the rest go through their own path, each as its own command. `requested` means the command was accepted, not that it took effect. Needs ticket.update on each Ticket's Project for Change owner and Change priority, run.control for Pause outcome and ticket.read for Snooze; an item the caller may not change is answered per item, never as a refusal of the request.

422.description: BULK_ACTION_UNKNOWN: the action is not one of change_owner, change_priority, snooze, pause_outcome. There is no bulk approval: an approval binds a person to one revision and its evidence, so approval stays on the Ticket. INPUT_INVALID: the request is malformed, or params leaves out what the action needs (owner_user_id, priority or until).

default.description: An error, in the public error shape.

post.summary: Preview a bulk action on Inbox decisions
post.description: Say, for each of 1 to 100 waiting decisions, what Change owner, Change priority, Snooze or Pause outcome would do to it: will_change, no_effect (nothing to change) or not_allowed (you may not, or its state does not allow it), with the sentence to show and the item_digest to apply it with. Each item is computed for that item: owner and priority on the decision's Ticket, Pause outcome on the decision's outcome through its pause_outcome action and Snooze on your own reminders through snooze_reminders, with params.until as the time. A decision that is no longer open has no effect. Writes nothing. Needs ticket.update on each Ticket's Project for Change owner and Change priority, run.control for Pause outcome and ticket.read for Snooze; an item the caller may not change is answered per item, never as a refusal of the request.

422.description: BULK_ACTION_UNKNOWN: the action is not one of change_owner, change_priority, snooze, pause_outcome. There is no bulk approval: an approval binds a person to one revision and its evidence, so approval stays on the Ticket. INPUT_INVALID: the request is malformed, or params leaves out what the action needs (owner_user_id, priority or until).

get.summary: Read the signed-in session's remaining time
get.description: The browser session this request carries, with the time it ends: expires_at, the earlier of idle_expires_at and absolute_expires_at, plus both limits and the server's current time. Reading this route never counts as activity: it moves neither the idle limit nor the last-used time, so polling it does not extend the session. It answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED without a live session.

default.description: An error, in the public error shape.

post.description: Push the browser session's idle limit out to now plus the idle timeout, capped at the absolute limit: the absolute limit never moves. Like every unsafe auth request it is CSRF-protected (an allowed Origin and the X-CSRF-Token header). The session rotates to a new id — the token that made the call stops authenticating and the response carries the replacement cookie — and the answer is the same payload as the status read. It answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED for a dead session and 403 without a valid CSRF token.

default.description: An error, in the public error shape.

post.summary: Propose an addition to a contract
post.description: Propose an addition to a contract: multipart `file`, a fragment in the contract's format holding only the operations being added or changed (and repeated `files` beside it, as for a publish). It is converted like a publish and recorded as a proposed revision whose operations come from the fragment, accepted under the Account's Contract approval. The answer says which operations become pending (not yet in the newest published revision) and which are already landed. With `dry_run` it answers the same and records nothing. A refused fragment answers its errors and is not announced. Requires contract.revise: a Contributor or Manager of the provider Project, a maintainer of the provider Domain, or an Owner or Administrator.

get.description: The Tickets board of a Domain of the Account named by X-PIDGEN-Account, across the Projects it covers (those of every Domain below it included) that the caller can open. The Domain owns no ticket: the read writes nothing and reorders no list. `open` holds every open card, in the Domain's order (priority, then the place of the card's list row in its own Project's list, then the Project key, then the root id), and the rows `GET /tickets?open=true` lists for those Projects. `counts` are the Project board's Filter counts over those Projects, finished work included, plus `project` (by Project id) and `subdomain` (by the id of a Domain directly below this one); `project` and `subdomain` filter like the other groups. `finished` pages the finished cards the filters leave, most recently finished first, `limit` at a time, as card rows. `projects` names every Project a card belongs to. `hidden_open` counts the open Stories and Tasks in covered Projects the caller can't open, whatever the filters; nothing else about them is returned. Requires domain.read. An unknown Domain, another Account's, and one the caller may not read is 404 DOMAIN_NOT_FOUND. The Account domain's board is over every Project of the Account, and its `subdomain` group offers the live Domains with no live parent, which sit directly under it.

post.summary: Publish a spec file a Domain provides
post.description: Publish a spec file: multipart `file` (the entry) and, for a spec split over several files, repeated `files`, each named by its path relative to the entry's directory; at most 200 files and 8 MiB in all. The file is converted with no person or model: its format detected (OpenAPI 2.0, 3.0, 3.1; AsyncAPI 2.x, 3.x), its $refs resolved inside the files sent, validated, and its operations indexed. A contract is identified by its provider and `source_path`: the first publish creates it, a changed file records its next published revision (additive, or breaking when an operation or a type its operations reach is removed, or `breaking` is true), and the same interface again answers `unchanged` and records nothing. The answer names the pending operations the publish lands. A revision is accepted under the Account's Contract approval. With `dry_run` it answers the same and records and announces nothing. A refusal that is not a dry run is kept, answers its `refusal_id` in details, and is announced in the Inbox to the publisher and the provider's people with the refused file; the same file refused again is only counted, and a later successful publish of the path resolves it. `domain_id` is the Domain's id (DOM-...); the Domain's home provides the contract. Requires contract.revise on the Domain: a maintainer of it, or an Owner or Administrator; the Account's plan must include Domains.

CONTRACT_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED: it is not OpenAPI (2.0, 3.0, 3.1) or AsyncAPI (2.x, 3.x). CONTRACT_EXTERNAL_REF: a $ref is a URL, an absolute path or a path that leaves the files sent. CONTRACT_CONVERSION_TIMEOUT: converting it took longer than 60 seconds and was stopped. Each lists every error (up to 100) in details.errors, each {message, location}, location null when there is none. INPUT_INVALID: the request failed validation.

get.summary: List a Domain's Epics with the work under them
get.description: List the Domain Epics of a Domain of the Account named by X-PIDGEN-Account, with only the work under them, and each Epic's members grouped by Project. Members come from every Project the Domain covers; those in Projects the caller can't open, with the work under them, are only counted in the entry's `hidden`. `state=open` (the default) lists every open Domain Epic, oldest first, with the running count of the covered Projects the caller can open; `page` and `per_page` do not apply. `state=finished` lists a page of the completed and cancelled ones, the most recently finished first, 10 a page by default. The Domain Epics of every Domain below it are included, each naming its Domain, unless `subdomains=false`. Every Epic and ticket is the row `GET /tickets` lists. Requires domain.read. An unknown Domain, another Account's, and one the caller may not read is 404 DOMAIN_NOT_FOUND.

The simulation admits work as the scheduler does -- by priority, then the Project's list, waiting on dependencies, within the Project's capacity inside the Account's, never interrupting running work -- and draws each unfinished ticket's duration from the Project's completed work of the last 60 days. With too little history an Epic's reason is none_yet; an Epic with no members has reason no_members. Requires ticket.read. post.description: Steer a session: the guidance is aimed at the session's step and queued for that step's next prompt, which is the next turn of the session or, if the session has ended, the step's next attempt. It is rendered into exactly one prompt and never sent to another step. It reads `queued`, then `delivered` when a worker claims the job carrying it, then `acknowledged` when that job's result comes back; it reads `unapplied` (`step_not_run_again`) when the run settles without the step running again. A steer to a session that ended while its step will run again is accepted. Sending again with the same `idempotency_key` as the same author returns the first instruction. `artifact_refs` pins the exact versions of existing artifacts of the Ticket's outcome, and `upload_ids` claims staged uploads as the Ticket's input artifacts and pins them, at most 10 together; the prompt that receives the steer names exactly those versions, even after a newer version is uploaded. `mode` is `steer` (the default) or `queue`. Quotes are provenance only and are checked before anything is written: `source_message_ids` must be messages of the Ticket's conversation, `quoted_event_refs` events of its sessions, and `quoted_file_refs` lines whose digest matches the Ticket's change snapshot with that commit or the preview its workstation reports for the current turn. Needs run.control (and artifact.upload for `upload_ids`).

NO_CONTROLLABLE_RUN: the session has no run.

QUOTE_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: a quoted message, event, snapshot or preview that is not the Ticket's or cannot be read. QUOTE_DIGEST_MISMATCH: quoted file lines that are not in that diff or do not match their digest. An upload is refused with ticket creation's codes (UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND, FILE_TOO_LARGE, ...).

post.description: Create a Ticket in Backlog in a Project of the Account named by X-PIDGEN-Account. The creator is the caller. `kind: epic` creates an Epic: the Project's next ticket number, the Account's Unassigned Agent, the `epic-delivery` workflow type, its `description` as objective, and its branch checked on the Project's forge (a new name must be free, a target must exist) but not cut. `kind: epic` with `domain_id` instead of `project_id` creates a Domain Epic in the Domain's home, numbered from the Domain's key, always on the Project base (it owns no branch); it needs `domain_epic.create` on the Domain and the Domains feature, and a Domain that covers at least one Project. `parent_ticket_id` creates the Ticket in an Epic of the same Project. With `start_refinement`, START_REFINEMENT is submitted once the Ticket is committed: `refinement_command_id` names the command, and `command_error` says why refinement did not start — the Ticket is created either way. An invalid body is 422 INPUT_INVALID.

Approving a delivery review while a MUST acceptance criterion is not passing for that revision is MUST_CRITERIA_NOT_PASSING (409, error.details.instead approve_with_exception, error.details.unproven_criteria) under either approval mode; approve with exception_reason is an approval with exception, which records the reason and the criteria it was given without (their status is unchanged). An empty exception_reason is EXCEPTION_REASON_REQUIRED (422). Under automatic approval the person approving is recorded as the approver. Under manual approval, approving (with or without exception_reason) while a requested change of the latest request is unresolved is REQUESTED_CHANGE_UNRESOLVED (409, error.details.unresolved_item_ids); see GET /api/v1/tickets/{ticket_id}/review/return. Automatic approval is unaffected.

REQUESTED_CHANGE_UNRESOLVED: under manual approval, a requested change is unresolved ("Approval is withheld while a requested change is unresolved."); request changes again. REJECT_RETIRED: reject on a delivery review; request changes, or cancel the Ticket.

The rework pass's acceptance verification checks each line as an extra target beside the acceptance criteria and reports a verdict at the commit it tested: passed is `verified`, failed is `unresolved`, unverifiable or not reported is `unknown`; each `evidence` entry names the `revision` it was tested at. These extra targets never change a criterion's status and never count for automatic approval. `agent_account` is the implementing agent's note on the line when its result has one. `outside_request` lists changed files no requested change addresses; they never withhold approval. Under manual approval, while a requested change is `unresolved`, `approval_withheld` is true and approving is refused 409 REQUESTED_CHANGE_UNRESOLVED ("Approval is withheld while a requested change is unresolved."); automatic approval is unaffected and `approval_withheld_reason` says why. get.description: Read one Ticket's runs, node attempts, sessions and token subtotals, from the analytics facts, for a Ticket of the Account named by X-PIDGEN-Account, by its key (e.g. WEB-1) or internal id. Runs follow the Ticket's run chain and list their node attempts; every subtotal is a known-usage sum over turns with its token and split coverage beside it. Every attempt and subtotal carries uncached input, so uncached input, cache write, cache read and output add up to total. Each attempt carries its cost, the basis that priced it (reported, account_price, list_price or unavailable) and the price version; a subtotal sums the priced attempts and is cost_partial when any is unpriced, never counting it as zero. automatic_rework marks the attempts of loops a failed check started inside their run, and each subtotal carries their tokens and cost. A root with descendants also reports its lineage separately, never added to its own subtotal. Wall time is the Ticket's elapsed window, not a sum of node durations. for resolve_target_conflict, the target ref and the tip the repair merges (target_ref, target_tip), the branch and its head, the conflicting files when known, the checks it re-runs, where it redelivers, and the workspace and history it keeps; for cancel_ticket, the Tickets cancelled and the dependents left blocked, the workspace, the disposition, superseded_by, retain_workspace and close_pull_request it applies, the pull request as the forge reports it (pull_request: url, number, state), the pending commands it supersedes (supersedes) and the Ticket's latest delivery operation (delivery_operation); for retry_pull_request_close and leave_pull_request_open, the pull request, the forge's refusal and whether it closes it (closes); for check_publication_status, the operation whose result is unknown (operation) and that it starts no push (starts_push: false); for sync_comments, the pull request whose comments it reads again (pull_request: url, number, state); for reposition and reprioritize, the priority before and after (priority: from, to; changes_priority), whether the Ticket holds a place in its Project's list (in_project_list) and moves in it (moves), and the Tickets it lands right after (after) and right before (before), null at either end; for convert_to_tag, the tag it applies (tag: name, the Epic's title; tag_id and exists for a tag of that name the Project already has, which is reused), the members it tags and detaches from the Epic (members: ticket_id, ticket_key, title) and the Epic it abandons (abandons: ticket_id, ticket_key); for pause_outcome, the Ticket's stage (stage), the live runs of its outcome asked to pause at their next safe boundary (running: run_id, kind refinery or execution), whether a pending automatic start is suspended (suspends_automatic_start) and whether a push in flight must settle first (push_in_flight); for resume_outcome, the stage and the runs it resumes (resumes); for terminate_run with stop_for_rework, stop_for_rework and the stage the Ticket returns to (ticket_stage_after); for snooze_reminders, the time chosen (until), the snooze it replaces (replaces) and the escalation and hold times it leaves where they are (escalate_at, hold_at); for defer_decision, the new date (deferred_until), the number of deferrals it makes (deferral_count), the latest date a deferral may be (latest) and the ladder it restarts from the new date (ladder: remind_at, escalate_at, hold_at); for hold_decision, what stops -- the decision's Ticket and the Tickets that depend on it (held: ticket_id, ticket_key, title) -- what continues (continues: the Ticket's other siblings), the runs asked to pause at a safe boundary (runs_to_pause) and when the hold is reviewed (review_at, review_after_days, time_zone); for a decision_override, how the label is applied (mechanism: override, while none of the step's dependents has started, else redecide), the label and the steps that run again (runs_again); for remove_dependency, the prerequisite and its stage; for retry_admission, the refusal it retries (finding_code, cause_code, detail); for return_to_planning, stops (the run_id and sessions that end at a safe boundary, none from Ready), withdraws_readiness (whether the Ticket's admission is withdrawn) and kept (the workspace_branch, the plan_digest, the accepted_children and the number of recorded_answers it keeps); for start_work, exactly four checks in this order (checks: check, passed, detail), plan_current, criteria_set, agent_assigned, workflow_configured -- complexity is never a check; a failed check refuses the execute START_CHECKS_FAILED, naming each failed check in error.details.failed_checks -- what admission will still wait for, as a sentence (not_checked), the approval mode that will apply (approval_mode), the merge policy that will apply and where it is set (merge_policy: value, and source ticket, epic or project) and how many pieces of work are scheduled (pieces_of_work); for plan_work, the stage the Ticket moves to (stage_to: research_needed); for ask_before_starting and correct_plan_decision, the plan's revision (revision) and its decisions (decisions: question, chosen, alternatives, and conflicts -- the quotes of the request the plan's choice may contradict, each with whether it was verified); correct_plan_decision also names the stage the Ticket moves to (stage_to) and, once it is given its plan_correction, the answers it would record (answers); for approve_delivery, approve_with_exception and request_delivery_changes, the head commit under review (reviewed_revision), the MUST criteria not passing for it (unproven_criteria: criterion_index, criterion_id, priority, statement, status, unverifiable, verifier_note) and the gate it answers (gate: workflow_run_id, node_id, gate_id, gate_generation); the two approvals also name the criterion overrides they rely on (overrides_relied_on) and whether the person, not the automatic approval policy, is recorded as the approver (approver_replaces_policy: true under automatic approval), and approve_with_exception the reason it records (exception_reason); request_delivery_changes of a delivered pull request (closed without merging, or still open) instead names the pull request and the state the forge reported (pull_request, pull_request_state), the stage the Ticket returns to (stage_to: in_execution), that history is kept, and where the rework redelivers (redelivery: pull_request, branch, new_pull_request: false -- the same branch, so new commits push to the same pull request); for override_acceptance_criterion, the criterion (criterion: criterion_index, criterion_id, priority, statement), its status now and the one given (from_status, to_status), the verifier's own result, which stays visible (verifier_status, unverifiable, evidence), the revision the override applies to (revision), whether it counts for the evidence gate (counts_for_evidence_gate: a MUST criterion to passing) and whether automatic approval follows it (automatic_approval_follows). Each workstation choice shows the parked run (run_id), its worker (workstation, worker_name, offline_since) and whether someone already chose to wait (waiting): for relocate_run, that the run continues from its last durable point and may repeat work only the absent worker held (continues, may_repeat); for wait_for_worker, that the outage auto-release is held (holds_auto_release); for retry_provisioning, the worker that refused the moved work (refused_by), the delivered commits it named (lost_commits: commit, ticket_id, title, stage) and that none is discarded (discards_commits: false); for start_from_remote_branch, the same, that they are discarded, and the child Tickets reopened to redo them (reopens); for close_completed, the delivery (delivery_id, delivery_kind, pull_request, branch), that its landing is recorded on your acknowledgement and the stage it reaches (stage_after); for reapply_delivery, the delivery, the verification it is checked again with and the stage it reaches; for attribute_workspace_residue, the worker's report (workspace_id, head_sha, status_digest, paths), recorded with no path assigned (unassigned_paths) and nothing deleted (deletes: false). For lift_provider_pause, the subscription (harness, provider), the pauses it ends in both windows (pauses), whether this Ticket is released (ticket_released), the other Tickets released in Projects where the caller can act (other_tickets) and how many more elsewhere in the Account (other_tickets_elsewhere), and what happens if the provider still refuses (if_still_refused).

confirmable.title: Confirmable
confirmable.description: False when the action waits on a prerequisite (prerequisite): its effects are shown in full, and executing it is refused with the prerequisite's code until it is met. True otherwise.

ActionPreviewResult.title: ActionPreviewResult
ActionPreviewResult.description:
A previewed action.

Execute it with `POST /api/v1/tickets/{ticket_id}/actions/execute`, sending this
preview_digest, the same action and target, and every required acknowledgement.

kind.description: What the action acts on.

run_id.title: Run Id

node_id.title: Node Id

fan_out_key.title: Fan Out Key

prerequisite_id.title: Prerequisite Id
prerequisite_id.description: For a dependency target: the prerequisite Ticket the dependency is on.

decision_key.title: Decision Key
decision_key.description: For a decision target: the decision's key, as an attention item carries it.

criterion_index.title: Criterion Index
criterion_index.description: For a criterion target: the criterion's zero-based position in the Ticket's acceptance_criteria; null for every other target.

ActionTarget.title: ActionTarget
ActionTarget.description: The Ticket, run or step an action acts on.

source_id.title: Source Id
source_id.description: The prerequisite Ticket: its key (e.g. WEB-2) or internal id.

dep_type.description: How this Ticket depends on the source.

AddTicketDependencyRequest.title: AddTicketDependencyRequest
AddTicketDependencyRequest.description: A prerequisite to declare: this Ticket depends on `source_id`.

AdminCommandAction.title: AdminCommandAction
AdminCommandAction.description: Actions accepted by the universal command boundary.

AdmissionBlockerProjection.title: AdmissionBlockerProjection
AdmissionBlockerProjection.description:
One open pre-run blocker rendered consistently on list and detail views.

Starting the Ticket again is its ``retry_admission`` action, decided with its others.

AgentCommand.title: AgentCommand
AgentCommand.description:
A command on an Agent: its request, disposition and convergence timestamps.

`status` is `applied` or `refused`; a refusal names its `disposition_code` and carries
the sentence a person reads as `disposition_detail.message`.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

AgentCommandResponse.title: AgentCommandResponse
AgentCommandResponse.description: The command an Agent change was recorded as.

question_id.title: Question Id
question_id.description: The question's id, e.g. `q1`; an alternative to `question_index`.

question_index.title: Question Index
question_index.description: The 0-based index of the question in the request's list; an alternative to `question_id`.

outcome.description: `answer` records your answer; `use_recommendation` records the question's recommended answer as your assumption; `ask_teammate` asks `ask_user_id` to answer it; `leave_open` records that you left it open. Only `answer` settles a question with your own words; the others leave it for someone else or for Create anyway.

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: Your answer. Required for the `answer` outcome.

ask_user_id.title: Ask User Id
ask_user_id.description: The teammate to ask, with `ask_teammate`: someone who may answer in the request's Project.

AnswerItem.title: AnswerItem
AnswerItem.description:
What the caller does with one question: answer it, or say they cannot.

Name the question by `question_id` or by `question_index`, never both.

AnswerOutcome.title: AnswerOutcome
AnswerOutcome.description: What a person does with one question.

current.title: Current
current.description: The version this service speaks, MAJOR.MINOR.

minimum.title: Minimum
minimum.description: The oldest version still served, MAJOR.MINOR.

ApiVersionWindow.title: ApiVersionWindow
ApiVersionWindow.description: The PIDGEN-API-Version values this service accepts.

entry_id.title: Entry Id
entry_id.description: A comment, reply or answer of the thread.

include_replies.title: Include Replies
include_replies.description: With a comment: apply its replies too (the thread).

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: A requested change of an earlier request.

ApplySourceRequest.title: ApplySourceRequest
ApplySourceRequest.description: What to apply to the draft: one conversation entry, or one requested change.

ApplyStatus.title: ApplyStatus
ApplyStatus.description: Where an accepted apply stands: `applied` (settled) or `applying` (poll status_url).

name.title: Name
name.description: The tag's name, 1 to 50 characters once trimmed. A name the Ticket's Project already has, in any case, applies that tag; a new name creates the tag with the palette's next colour.

ApplyTagRequest.title: ApplyTagRequest
ApplyTagRequest.description: A tag to apply to a Ticket, by name.

ApprovalMode.title: ApprovalMode
ApprovalMode.description:
How a ticket's approval gates get resolved.

The mode is chosen when the work is submitted — on an intent or on a ticket —
and is never inferred. ``AUTO`` resolves only the gates that are eligible for
it; clarification gates and every deterministic quality gate are untouched,
and all human oversight moves to the delivered pull request.

version.title: Version
version.description: Which version of the artifact this is.

available.title: Available
available.description: False when this version can no longer be read: shown as `Unavailable attachment`.

ArtifactPin.title: ArtifactPin
ArtifactPin.description: One artifact version attached to or pinned by an entry.

ArtifactReference.title: ArtifactReference
ArtifactReference.description: An existing ticket artifact to attach.

AttentionAddressee.title: AttentionAddressee
AttentionAddressee.description:
A person or shared queue responsible for a decision.

``delegate``: the decision was delegated to ``user_id`` (its owner is unchanged).
``reviewer``: a hold review, addressed to the Project's Managers, else the Account's
Owners and Administrators.

on_hold.title: On Hold
on_hold.description: Open hold reviews in your review scope; 0 when you review no holds.

AttentionCounts.title: AttentionCounts
AttentionCounts.description: Counts before view and Project filtering; each decision counts once.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: The Ticket's Project.

code.title: Code
code.description: What is wrong, as a stable code. For example `workstation_offline`: the Ticket's run waits on a worker that went offline mid-run; it is addressed to the Ticket's effective owner, and its actions are `relocate_run` (recommended) and `wait_for_worker` -- or, after the new worker refused the moved work, `retry_provisioning`, `start_from_remote_branch` and `wait_for_worker`.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: What is wrong, for a person to read.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The workflow run concerned, if any.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: The agent session concerned, if any.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The workflow node concerned, if any.

first_detected_at.title: First Detected At
first_detected_at.description: When the finding was first seen.

last_seen_at.title: Last Seen At
last_seen_at.description: When the finding was last confirmed.

cause_code.title: Cause Code
cause_code.description: For a Ticket blocked on workspace preparation: the failure's code; retrying the admission is its `retry_admission` action.

snapshot_id.title: Snapshot Id
snapshot_id.description: For a worker that went offline mid-run: the last durable snapshot of the Ticket's work that the run continues from if it is moved; null when none was recorded.

effect_safety.title: Effect Safety
effect_safety.description: For a parked node: whether its effects are safe to repeat.

recovery_reason.title: Recovery Reason
recovery_reason.description: For a parked node: why it parked.

workflow_attention.title: Workflow Attention
workflow_attention.description: For a run's workflow attention: its resolution class, violations, questions and remediation. What a person may do about it is `actions`.

addressee.description: The person or shared queue responsible for this decision.

claim.description: Current claimant, or null when unclaimed.

live_run_hold.description: The holding runs and the scheduler's explanation.

target.description: What this decision is about -- a step, a run, a dependency or the Ticket -- and so what its actions were decided for.

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: Every action decided for `target`: each with whether it is allowed (with the typed refusal and its sentence when not), whether you may take it, whether it is recommended and why, and what it would do. Render these instead of deriving an action from the finding's code.

asks.title: Asks
asks.description: What this decision asks of a person besides its actions: answer_questions, review_delivery, confirm_plan, request_delivery_changes, inspect_rejected_attempt, replace_child_plan, change_prompt_configuration, inspect_evidence, open_worker, review_hold (a hold review: keep holding or cancel), assign_agent (a plan with no Agent: assign one, then start the work) or accept_contract (a contract revision waiting to be accepted; listed in contract_decisions, never on a finding). Render these instead of deriving a form from the finding's code.

followup.description: How this decision is followed up: reminded, escalated, then held. Set for a clarification, a delivery review, a hold review and a plan waiting for a person (a plan that contradicts the request, or one to start); null for every other kind.

hold.description: The active hold the decision caused, or the hold a hold review is about; null when there is none. `requested` until every affected run is observed at a safe boundary.

unproven_criteria.title: Unproven Criteria
unproven_criteria.description: For an evidence decision (code evidence_decision: automatic or manual approval of a delivery stopped at an unproven MUST criterion): each MUST criterion not passing for the revision under review. Null otherwise.

reviewed_revision.title: Reviewed Revision
reviewed_revision.description: For a delivery review: the head commit it reviews. Null otherwise, or when the head is not known yet.

test_suite.description: For test_suite_failing (the failed test nodes, their logs and the implementer's explanation) and test_suite_unavailable (the node that could not run and its last error), with the next action. Null for every other kind.

AttentionFinding.title: AttentionFinding
AttentionFinding.description: A Ticket needing a person's decision, and the repair on offer.

counts.description: Counts for every view before filtering.

following.title: Following
following.description: Followed work, only in the following view; excludes work waiting on you.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: The findings: those with a recommended action first, then newest first.

swept_at.title: Swept At
swept_at.description: When the audit sweep last ran; an empty queue is clean only since then.

review_scope.description: Whose holds you review in the on_hold view: account for an Account Owner or Administrator, projects (the Projects you manage) for a Project Manager, null for everyone else, for whom on_hold lists nothing.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: Always empty: waiting requests are no longer listed one by one but as request_items. A request waiting on its submitter is their needs_information item, and a waiting_requests item of its space's triagers. Kept for the published shape.

request_counts.description: Counts of requests for every view before filtering. The Inbox badge and its `n need you` count `counts.me` plus `request_counts.me` plus `request_counts.items`.

request_items.title: Request Items
request_items.description: Request items, in the me and all views (none in the others), those that need you first, then newest first: one grouped item per target space you triage while it has new requests (N new requests in <space>), updated as requests arrive and leave new, and one informational item per space you triage while requests there wait on their requester; for your own requests, needs_information while one waits on you and an informational item when one is promoted, resolved or closed; for those who manage the Account's request sources, one item per paused source until it resumes.

contract_notices.title: Contract Notices
contract_notices.description: Your unseen contract notices, newest first, listed beside the findings in the me and all views (none in the others): each contract change announced to you as the provider Project's Manager or provider Domain's maintainer, the contract's owner or the owner of linked work whose operations changed. A notice offers no action and asks nothing; mark it seen with POST /api/v1/attention/notices/{notice_id}/seen. It never blocks work.

contract_decisions.title: Contract Decisions
contract_decisions.description: Contract revisions waiting to be accepted (Contract approval breaking or all), one decision per revision, oldest first: in me those addressed to you, in all every one of the Projects you can read, none in the others. Each asks accept_contract; Accept is its accept route. Gone once accepted.

contract_refusals.title: Contract Refusals
contract_refusals.description: The refused publishes of spec files you were told of and have not marked seen, newest first, in the me and all views (none in the others): told to the person who published and the provider's Project Managers or Domain maintainers, and the contract's owner. Each lists the first errors with their locations and downloads the refused file; a later successful publish of the path resolves it. It offers no action and asks nothing; mark it seen with POST /api/v1/attention/contract-refusals/{refusal_id}/seen.

AttentionQueue.title: AttentionQueue
AttentionQueue.description: The Account's open findings needing a person, with the repair each offers.

decision_key.title: Decision Key
decision_key.description: The request's identity as a decision that waits for a person; the same as `request.decision_key`.

request.description: The request: its questions, who it is addressed to, how it is followed up and what the caller may do with it.

AttentionRequest.title: AttentionRequest
AttentionRequest.description:
A request that waits for answers, listed beside the findings: a decision for a person.

It is not a finding: a request has no Ticket yet, so it was listed in `requests` and
never in `findings`. No request is listed this way any more: a waiting request is a
request item (`RequestInboxItem`).

kind.description: What the Ticket is: `task` (the default), `story`, or `epic`, a delivery program that holds Stories and Tasks and does no work of its own. An Epic is numbered like any Ticket, takes the Account's Unassigned Agent and the `epic-delivery` workflow type, and refuses `team_member_id`, `workflow_type` (other than `epic-delivery`), `approval_mode`, `acceptance_criteria`, `start_refinement`, `required_capabilities`, `estimated_complexity` and `epic_id` (422 EPIC_FIELD_REFUSED). An Epic's `parent_ticket_id` may name only a Domain Epic (else 422 EPIC_HAS_NO_PARENT). An Epic sent `domain_id` is a Domain Epic.

parent_ticket_id.title: Parent Ticket Id
parent_ticket_id.description: The Epic to create the Ticket in, by id or key: a Project Epic of the same Project (else 422 PARENT_PROJECT_MISMATCH), or a Domain Epic whose domain covers the Ticket's Project, directly or through a subdomain (else 422 PARENT_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN). A Ticket is created only in an Epic: an Epic's only parent is a Domain Epic (422 EPIC_HAS_NO_PARENT), a task has no children (422 TASK_HAS_NO_CHILDREN), and a story gains children through its plan (422 PARENT_NOT_EPIC). Omitted, the Ticket has no parent.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: What the work must achieve. Required, except for an Epic, which may send `description` instead.

description.title: Description
description.description: An Epic's description, stored as its objective; send it or `objective`, not both. Only an Epic takes it (422 EPIC_ONLY_FIELD).

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: An Epic's target date. Only an Epic takes it (422 EPIC_ONLY_FIELD).

branch_mode.description: Where an Epic's members deliver, fixed at creation; only an Epic takes it (422 EPIC_ONLY_FIELD). `project_base` (the default): the Project's base branch; `feature_branch` must be empty. `create_new`: a new branch named `feature_branch`, or derived from the title (epic/<slug>, suffixed when taken); the name must be free on the Project's forge, and the branch is cut from the latest Project base when a member first needs it, not now. `target`: the existing branch named `feature_branch`, reused as it is; it must exist on the forge. Both branch modes need the Project's Forge Connection.

feature_branch.title: Feature Branch
feature_branch.description: An Epic's branch name for `create_new` (optional) or `target` (required). Only an Epic takes it (422 EPIC_ONLY_FIELD).

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Target project as a reference: its id (e.g. proj-pidgen) or its prefix (e.g. PIDGEN), resolved in the request's Account. Required, unless `domain_id` is sent: omitting both is 422 PROJECT_REQUIRED.

domain_id.title: Domain Id
domain_id.description: Create a Domain Epic: the Domain as a reference, its id (DOM-…) or its key (e.g. COM), resolved in the request's Account (else 404 DOMAIN_NOT_FOUND). Only an Epic takes it (422 EPIC_ONLY_FIELD). It replaces `project_id`: the Epic is created in the Domain's home and numbered from the Domain's key (e.g. COM-12); sending both is 422 DOMAIN_PROJECT_CONFLICT. A Domain Epic never owns a branch, so `branch_mode` and `feature_branch` are refused with it (422 EPIC_FIELD_REFUSED, error.details.field). A Domain that covers no Project is refused (422 DOMAIN_HAS_NO_PROJECTS). It needs `domain_epic.create` on the Domain (a Domain Maintainer, an Owner or an Administrator; else 403 FORBIDDEN) and the Account's Domains feature (else 403 ENTITLEMENT_LIMIT_REACHED).

team_member_id.title: Team Member Id
team_member_id.description: Agent assignment, an active Agent of the request's Account, including its reserved Unassigned Agent. An explicit selection overrides the Project default; null or omission selects the Project's default Agent, or the Account's Unassigned Agent when the Project names none.

epic_id.title: Epic Id
epic_id.description: The Epic to file the Ticket under: the epic-kind Ticket's key (e.g. PIDGEN-12) or internal id (TKT-…); the same as naming it in `parent_ticket_id`. A Ticket that is not an Epic is refused (422 PARENT_NOT_EPIC), a Project Epic of another Project too (422 EPIC_PROJECT_MISMATCH), and a Domain Epic whose domain does not cover the Project (422 PARENT_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN). An Epic takes no `epic_id`.

workflow_type.title: Workflow Type
workflow_type.description: A registered workflow type key; GET /api/v1/workflow-types lists them. An unregistered key is refused with 422 UNKNOWN_WORKFLOW_TYPE.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Priority, P0 (most urgent) to P4. Omitted, it is P2, or the `after` Ticket's priority when `after` is given, or else the Domain Epic's priority for a Ticket filed directly under a Domain Epic. An integer 1 to 10 is the legacy scale and is read as its level: 1-2 P1, 3-5 P2, 6-7 P3, 8-10 P4.

after.title: After
after.description: Place the Ticket right after this one (an id or key) in its Project's list, which is ordered by priority, then position. The anchor must be in the same Project and hold a row of its list (no parent, or a Domain Epic as parent), and the priority must fit there: between the anchor's and the next Ticket's. Omitted, the Ticket goes to the end of its priority. A Ticket inside a Project Epic holds no row; one directly under a Domain Epic holds one in its own Project's list.

acceptance_criteria.title: Acceptance Criteria
acceptance_criteria.description: Acceptance criteria. Each needs only a statement; `assertion` and the pinned check `test_assertion` are optional. The planning gate needs at least one criterion with a non-empty statement.

context_artifacts.title: Context Artifacts
context_artifacts.description: Lightweight textual references only. Files and images are claimed through `artifact_upload_ids`, never placed in the ticket body.

artifact_upload_ids.title: Artifact Upload Ids
artifact_upload_ids.description: Opaque staged-upload capabilities (from POST /api/v1/artifact-uploads) to claim with this ticket. Only the opaque IDs are accepted — never bytes, host paths, storage references, or credentials.

approval_mode.description: How this ticket's approval gates resolve. Defaults to `auto`, which resolves eligible gates itself and leaves human oversight to the delivered pull request. Choose `manual` at creation to wait for a person at every approval gate.

merge_policy.description: Ticket-level merge policy: `manual`, `auto`, or `null` (default) to inherit the epic's, then the project's, policy. It only applies while the project has auto-merging enabled.

start_refinement.title: Start Refinement
start_refinement.description: Submit START_REFINEMENT after the Backlog Ticket commits.

CreateTicketRequest.title: CreateTicketRequest
CreateTicketRequest.description:
A Ticket to create in Backlog.

The creator is the caller; there is no `source_user`. An unknown field is refused
(422 INPUT_INVALID) rather than ignored.

url.title: Url
url.description: The URL to send to: `https` only, no user name, password or fragment, at most 2048 characters.

events.title: Events
events.description: The events to send: any of `attention.opened`, `attention.resolved`, `ticket.stage_changed`, `delivery.published` and `delivery.merged`; at least one.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: The Account the enrolled worker will belong to.

label.title: Label
label.description: The name given to the enrollment, if any.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Leading characters of the stored token hash.

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: The actor who created the enrollment.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the token stops being exchangeable.

consumed_at.title: Consumed At
consumed_at.description: When a worker exchanged it; null here.

state.title: State
state.description: `pending` when created.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: The worker's name.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.description: Whether the worker will be the Account fleet's.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: The scope the worker starts with; null takes the kind's default.

token.title: Token
token.description: The one-time pidgen_enroll_… token. Returned only in this response.

install_commands.description: The one-command install of each published form, keyed by form.

install.title: Install
install.description: Each published form of the worker with its install and enroll steps; show `eula` before running an install.

CreatedEnrollment.title: CreatedEnrollment
CreatedEnrollment.description: A new one-time enrollment token and how to install a worker with it; shown once.

id.title: Id
id.description: Opaque internal identity: 'TKT-' + 16 hex for new Tickets, the legacy {PREFIX}-{n} for Tickets created before the identity split. Joins, run ids and idempotency keys use this; humans never see it.

ticket_key.title: Ticket Key
ticket_key.description: Account-local public key {PREFIX}-{n}, e.g. PIDGEN-1. Every human-facing surface shows this; it equals id for legacy Tickets.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: Owning Account, taken from the Project at creation.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Project this ticket belongs to (required for new tickets).

team_member_id.title: Team Member Id
team_member_id.description: Assigned Agent, in the Ticket's Account. Unset, creation assigns the Account's reserved Unassigned Agent; a persisted Ticket always has one.

version.title: Version
version.description: Database-owned optimistic-concurrency token for governed Ticket mutations.

ticket_number.title: Ticket Number
ticket_number.description: Numeric part of the id, increments per project.

kind.description: Structural kind: `task` (a leaf), `story` (a parent; a Task becomes one when a child plan is materialized under it, before its execution starts) or `epic` (a delivery program). A bug is a `task` or `story` whose workflow_type is `bugfix`.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: An Epic's target date; null for a Story or Task.

branch_mode.description: Where an Epic's members deliver: `project_base`, `create_new` or `target`. Null for a Story or Task.

feature_branch.title: Feature Branch
feature_branch.description: An Epic's feature branch, fixed when the Epic is created; null for the Project base, and for a Story or Task.

feature_branch_cut_at.title: Feature Branch Cut At
feature_branch_cut_at.description: When an Epic's feature branch was cut on the forge; set means nothing is left to cut. A `target` branch, which already exists, records its creation time.

feature_branch_cut_error.title: Feature Branch Cut Error
feature_branch_cut_error.description: The forge's error from the last failed cut of an Epic's feature branch.

backlog_disposition.description: Why a high-level Ticket most recently entered Backlog.

execution_admission_digest.title: Execution Admission Digest
execution_admission_digest.description: Current human promotion digest; only valid on a high-level Ticket.

materialized_plan_digest.title: Materialized Plan Digest
materialized_plan_digest.description: Digest of the root Ticket's current materialized child plan.

approval_mode.description: How this ticket's approval gates resolve. `auto` is the creation default and resolves eligible gates itself; choose `manual` at creation to require human review at every gate.

merge_policy.description: Ticket-level merge policy. `null` inherits the Epic's, then the Project's policy; it only applies while the Project has auto-merging enabled.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Legacy priority, 1 (highest) to 10, kept in step with priority_level: P0 writes 1, P1 2, P2 5, P3 7 and P4 9. Read priority_level instead.

priority_level.description: Priority, 0 to 4 for P0 (most urgent) to P4. Default P2. The Project's list is ordered by priority, then list_position.

list_position.title: List Position
list_position.description: Rank key of a Ticket without a parent in its Project's list: within one priority, keys sort bytewise in list order. Null for a Ticket with a parent.

owner_user_id.title: Owner User Id
owner_user_id.description: Explicit human owner; null inherits the parent's owner or the root's submitter.

prompt_overrides.title: Prompt Overrides
prompt_overrides.description: Complete global-workflow and canonical prompt-node exception set for this Ticket.

prompt_overrides_digest.title: Prompt Overrides Digest
prompt_overrides_digest.description: Canonical digest fencing writes and run-acceptance snapshots.

target_lane.description: Lane this Ticket was asked to occupy once it leaves the Refinery. Persisted from the intent; a `ready_for_implementation` ticket is auto-promoted to IMPLEMENTATION_READY after the Refinery returns it to Backlog, subject to the promotion gate ladder.

auto_promotion_status.description: Outcome of a ready_for_implementation auto-promotion: `pending` while the Refinery runs, then `promoted` or `skipped`. `None` for the default backlog lane.

auto_promotion_reason.title: Auto Promotion Reason
auto_promotion_reason.description: Why a ready_for_implementation auto-promotion was skipped (the failing gate), or empty on success.

refinement_command_id.title: Refinement Command Id
refinement_command_id.description: The START_REFINEMENT command submitted for the Ticket when `start_refinement` was requested and the command service took it; null otherwise.

command_error.description: Why refinement did not start, when `start_refinement` was requested and the command was not submitted, refused or failed; null otherwise. The Ticket was created either way.

CreatedTicket.title: CreatedTicket
CreatedTicket.description: The Ticket just created in Backlog, and what became of its refinement request.

section.title: Section
section.description: The artifact section that covers this criterion.

CriterionEvidence.title: CriterionEvidence
CriterionEvidence.description: Where a criterion's verification evidence is: an artifact and its section.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status the person gave the criterion.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: The head revision the override was made on.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it was made.

verifier_status.title: Verifier Status
verifier_status.description: The verifier's own status for the criterion.

CriterionOverride.title: CriterionOverride
CriterionOverride.description:
A person's override of a criterion's status, beside the verifier's own result.

It applies to the revision it was made on: a new revision is verified again and the
override no longer counts. The verifier's status at the time is kept, so the verifier's
result stays visible and is never rewritten.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status the criterion is given.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the criterion's status is overridden.

CriterionOverrideChoice.title: CriterionOverrideChoice
CriterionOverrideChoice.description:
The status a person gives one criterion, and why (`override_acceptance_criterion`).

Required to execute. The override applies to the revision under review: a new revision
is verified again and the override no longer counts. Overriding a MUST criterion to
`passing` counts for automatic approval of that revision. Send the same choice to
preview and to execute: its digest covers it, and an execute with another one is
`PREVIEW_STALE`.

CriterionReportEntry.title: CriterionReportEntry
CriterionReportEntry.description:
What the implementer reported about one acceptance criterion, in its own words.

``criterion_id`` is the criterion's stable id. ``status`` is ``met`` (implemented and a
test proves it), ``unmet`` (not implemented, or its test fails) or ``uncovered``
(implemented, but no test proves it). It is never a verdict: the acceptance verifier
alone sets a criterion's status.

review_id.title: Review Id
review_id.description: The review's id (`CRV-…`); a flag's id when resolving.

criterion_id.title: Criterion Id
criterion_id.description: The criterion reviewed, by its stable id (`AC-…`).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `looks_right`: the person agrees with the criterion. `flag`: they raised a concern about it, in `note`.

note.title: Note
note.description: What the person said: required for a flag, null for most Looks right.

state.title: State
state.description: A flag's state: `open` until someone resolves it, then `resolved`. Null for Looks right.

mine.title: Mine
mine.description: Whether the review is the caller's own.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: The Conversation message the flag posted, quoting the criterion; its thread is the flag's discussion. Null for Looks right.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When the person made this review.

resolved_by.description: Who resolved the flag; null until then.

resolved_at.title: Resolved At
resolved_at.description: When the flag was resolved; null until then.

CriterionReview.title: CriterionReview
CriterionReview.description: One person's current review of one acceptance criterion.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `looks_right` to agree with the criterion; `flag` to raise a concern about it, which needs a `note`.

note.title: Note
note.description: What is wrong with the criterion, at most 4,000 characters. Required for a flag, and posted to the Ticket's Conversation quoting the criterion.

CriterionReviewRequest.title: CriterionReviewRequest
CriterionReviewRequest.description: Looks right, or a flag with a note.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

CriterionReviewResponse.title: CriterionReviewResponse
CriterionReviewResponse.description: One person's current review of one acceptance criterion.

reviews.title: Reviews
reviews.description: Every person's current review of the criterion, oldest first.

reviewed.title: Reviewed
reviewed.description: Whether anyone has reviewed the criterion.

looks_right.title: Looks Right
looks_right.description: How many people marked it Looks right.

flags.title: Flags
flags.description: How many people flagged it, open or resolved.

open_flags.title: Open Flags
open_flags.description: How many of its flags are open.

CriterionReviewSummary.title: CriterionReviewSummary
CriterionReviewSummary.description: One acceptance criterion's reviews and their counts.

writable.title: Writable
writable.description: Whether the criteria take reviews now: true while the Ticket is in Backlog or Ready. Elsewhere every write is refused with CRITERION_REVIEWS_CLOSED.

can_review.title: Can Review
can_review.description: Whether the caller may mark, flag and resolve now: `writable` and the caller has ticket.update.

reviewed.title: Reviewed
reviewed.description: How many criteria anyone has reviewed.

total.title: Total
total.description: How many acceptance criteria the Ticket has.

open_flags.title: Open Flags
open_flags.description: How many flags are open across the criteria.

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: Each acceptance criterion, in the Ticket's order, with its reviews.

CriterionReviews.title: CriterionReviews
CriterionReviews.description:
A Ticket's acceptance criteria with people's reviews: the section reads *2 of 3
reviewed · 1 open flag*. Reviews never hold promotion, Start work or approval.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

CriterionReviewsResponse.title: CriterionReviewsResponse
CriterionReviewsResponse.description: A Ticket's acceptance criteria with people's reviews.

claim_id.title: Claim Id
claim_id.description: Identity of this acquisition in the claim history.

decision_key.title: Decision Key
decision_key.description: Opaque identity from the attention item.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: The holder's display name.

DecisionClaim.title: DecisionClaim
DecisionClaim.description: The current holder of a decision; coordination grants no additional authority.

decision_key.title: Decision Key
decision_key.description: The decision's identity in the attention list.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What kind of decision is followed up.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The follow-up as a person reads it, its time in Account time, e.g. `Reminder sent to Sam · next: Escalate to Maya and the shared project queue · Fri 2 Oct at 09:12`.

waiting_on.description: The delegate, else the owner; null when the decision is addressed to the fallback chain.

owner.description: The decision's owner, if it has one.

delegated_by.description: Who delegated the decision, if anyone.

escalated_to.title: Escalated To
escalated_to.description: The people the decision was escalated to; empty before escalation.

next.description: The next step and its time, if any.

hold_at.title: Hold At
hold_at.description: When the decision reaches its hold point.

deferred_until.title: Deferred Until
deferred_until.description: Until when the decision is deferred.

deferral_count.title: Deferral Count
deferral_count.description: How many times the decision was deferred.

defer_latest.title: Defer Latest
defer_latest.description: The latest date Defer accepts now.

viewer_snoozed_until.title: Viewer Snoozed Until
viewer_snoozed_until.description: Until when your own reminders for this decision are snoozed.

time_zone.title: Time Zone
time_zone.description: Account time: the decision policy's time zone.

hold_id.title: Hold Id
hold_id.description: The hold the decision placed, if any.

DecisionFollowUp.title: DecisionFollowUp
DecisionFollowUp.description:
How a waiting decision is followed up: reminded, escalated, then held.

Time never rejects, approves or cancels a decision.

label.title: Label
label.description: One of the decision step's declared labels.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the decision is wrong for this Ticket.

DecisionOverrideChoice.title: DecisionOverrideChoice
DecisionOverrideChoice.description:
For replay_from_node of a decision step: the label a person decides it with.

The server chooses how the label is applied. While none of the step's dependents has
started, the step takes the label and routes on it (an override); once one has, the
step is re-decided by a replay that settles with the label and runs everything
downstream again. The preview names which (`effects.mechanism`: `override` or
`redecide`), and its digest covers the label and the reason.

DecisionOverrideRequest.title: DecisionOverrideRequest
DecisionOverrideRequest.description:
A human's replacement label for a decision node, carried by a re-decide replay.

The replayed attempt settles with `label` without asking the model, and the work
downstream runs again. `label` must be one the node declares; `reason` is required
and recorded with the recovery.

this_run.title: This Run
this_run.description: The version the run froze; null when it was not an authored version.

current_name.title: Current Name
current_name.description: The workflow a fresh run of the Ticket would use now; null when unknown. It differs from `name` when the Ticket's type was bound to another workflow.

current.title: Current
current.description: The active version of `current_name`; null when unknown.

adopts_current.title: Adopts Current
adopts_current.description: True when the action runs the current workflow; false when it keeps the run's.

DecisionWorkflow.title: DecisionWorkflow
DecisionWorkflow.description: Which version of the workflow a recovery runs: the run's own, or the current one.

DeletedMark.title: DeletedMark
DeletedMark.description: Who deleted a message and when: all the thread keeps of it.

show.title: Show
show.description: True when the tab shows the notification; false when it did not.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the tab did not show it. Required when `show` is false.

DeliverRequest.title: DeliverRequest
DeliverRequest.description: What the tab did with the notification.

workflow_run_id.title: Workflow Run Id
workflow_run_id.description: The run the attempt belongs to.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The step's id in the workflow.

fan_out_key.title: Fan Out Key
fan_out_key.description: The fan-out branch; null for a plain step.

DeliveredAttempt.title: DeliveredAttempt
DeliveredAttempt.description: The step attempt whose prompt received an instruction.

DeliveryKind.title: DeliveryKind
DeliveryKind.description: What reaching the destination meant for this ticket.

operation_id.title: Operation Id
operation_id.description: The operation's id, stable across its retries.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What the operation does.

ownership_generation.title: Ownership Generation
ownership_generation.description: The workspace ownership generation the worker held.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When it started, by the worker's clock.

observed_at.title: Observed At
observed_at.description: Its last observation, by the worker's clock.

state.title: State
state.description: `in_flight`, `settled`, or `unknown`: the worker lost the result and the push may have completed.

DeliveryOperation.title: DeliveryOperation
DeliveryOperation.description: A push, pull-request update or owner apply a worker reported for the Ticket.

name.title: Name
name.description: The worker's name as people read it.

DeliveryOperationWorker.title: DeliveryOperationWorker
DeliveryOperationWorker.description: The worker that performs a delivery operation.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

DeliveryResponse.title: DeliveryResponse
DeliveryResponse.description: The state the notification came to.

state.title: State
state.description: `sent`: the tab shows it. `obsolete`: its decision resolved. `suppressed`: routing, quiet hours or a snooze no longer allow it, or the tab did not show it.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why: `routed`, `resolved`, `quiet_hours`, ….

DeliveryResult.title: DeliveryResult
DeliveryResult.description: What taking the notification came to.

DepType.title: DepType
DepType.description:
How one Ticket depends on another.

`blocks`: the target may not execute until the source is completed. `informs`: the
source's outcome is useful context for the target, but does not hold it.
`parallel_safe`: the two may run at the same time.

DependencyCandidate.title: DependencyCandidate
DependencyCandidate.description: A Ticket this Ticket could be declared to depend on.

ticket_id.title: Ticket Id
ticket_id.description: The Ticket the prerequisite would be declared on.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: Tickets of the same Project that match the search and that declaring them as a prerequisite would accept, most recently created first.

DependencyCandidates.title: DependencyCandidates
DependencyCandidates.description: The Tickets a dependency declaration would accept as this Ticket's prerequisite.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

DependencyCandidatesResponse.title: DependencyCandidatesResponse
DependencyCandidatesResponse.description: The prerequisites the Ticket could be declared to depend on.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: The Account both endpoints belong to.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The internal id (TKT-…) of the Ticket that depends on the source.

dep_type.description: How the target depends on the source.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: The Project both endpoints belong to.

epic_id.title: Epic Id
epic_id.description: Retired: an edge carries no Epic label, so this is always null; the endpoints' Epics are their epic-kind ancestors.

DependencyEdge.title: DependencyEdge
DependencyEdge.description: A declared dependency edge: `target_id` depends on `source_id`.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

DependencyEdgeResponse.title: DependencyEdgeResponse
DependencyEdgeResponse.description: The dependency edge declared, or the one removed.

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: The internal id of the Ticket that waits for it.

DependencyGraphEdge.title: DependencyGraphEdge
DependencyGraphEdge.description: One declared `blocks` edge between two Tickets of the graph.

status_label.title: Status Label
status_label.description: The Ticket's lifecycle stage in the board's words: its `status.stage_label`, exactly as its own Ticket read reports it.

situation.description: The Ticket's situation, its `status.code` and `status.situation`, exactly as its own Ticket read reports them.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: How many `blocks` hops separate it from the Ticket the graph is centred on, by the shortest walk: negative for a prerequisite (-1 is a direct one), 0 for the Ticket itself, positive for a dependent (1 is a direct one).

on_critical_path.title: On Critical Path
on_critical_path.description: True when it lies on the longest chain of the centred Ticket's Epic, as the Epic's DAG computes it; false for every node when that Ticket has no Epic.

DependencyGraphNode.title: DependencyGraphNode
DependencyGraphNode.description: One Ticket of a ticket-centred dependency graph.

status_label.title: Status Label
status_label.description: The child's lifecycle stage in the board's words: its `status.stage_label`, exactly as its own Ticket read reports it.

DependencyGraphPiece.title: DependencyGraphPiece
DependencyGraphPiece.description: One of the centred Ticket's own pieces: a direct child.

DeploymentTier.title: DeploymentTier
DeploymentTier.description: The kind of environment an App Service process is deployed into.

device_code.title: Device Code
device_code.description: Secret the CLI polls with; never show it.

user_code.title: User Code
user_code.description: Code the person enters at verification_uri, XXXX-XXXX.

verification_uri.title: Verification Uri
verification_uri.description: Where the person approves the login.

verification_uri_complete.title: Verification Uri Complete
verification_uri_complete.description: verification_uri with the user code filled in.

DeviceAuthorizationIssued.title: DeviceAuthorizationIssued
DeviceAuthorizationIssued.description: A started login: what the CLI keeps and what it shows the person.

device_label.title: Device Label
device_label.description: A name for this device, shown when approving and in signed-in devices.

DeviceTokenResponse.title: DeviceTokenResponse
DeviceTokenResponse.description: The CLI token a device-code login issued.

DirectReviewResult.title: DirectReviewResult
DirectReviewResult.description: A synchronous review of a Ticket with no workflow runs.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Every Project a card of the board belongs to, by Project key.

hidden_open.title: Hidden Open
hidden_open.description: How many open Stories and Tasks sit in Projects the Domain covers that the caller can't open. The same whatever the filters; nothing else about them is returned.

DomainBoard.title: DomainBoard
DomainBoard.description:
The Tickets board of a Domain, across the Projects it covers. The Domain owns no
ticket: each card is its Project's, and its actions are that Project's.

epic.title: Epic
epic.description: By Epic id, and `none` for no Epic.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: By `story`, `task` and `bug`.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: By the Board's stage groups: Backlog, Planning, Ready, Executing, Review, Delivered and Failed.

member.title: Member
member.description: By Agent id, and `none` for no Agent.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: The cards the filters leave, open and finished.

subdomain.title: Subdomain
subdomain.description: By the id of a Domain directly below the board's Domain: the cards in the Projects it covers.

DomainBoardCounts.title: DomainBoardCounts
DomainBoardCounts.description:
Each Filter option's count over the Projects the Domain covers that the caller can open,
finished work included, by the Project board's rules, with two more groups.

An option's count is the number of cards left with that option the only one ticked in its
group and every other group as the request names it. A value no ticket carries is absent: its
count is 0. Work in Projects the caller can't open is in no count (see `hidden_open`).

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: Every open card's delivery-root id, in the Domain's order: the card's priority (P0 first), then the place of its list row (the root, or the Project Epic it sits in) in its own Project's list, then the Project key, then the root id. No order across Projects is stored; the Domain reorders no list.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.description: The rows `GET /tickets?open=true` lists for each of those Projects, newest first.

DomainBoardOpen.title: DomainBoardOpen
DomainBoardOpen.description: The open work of the Projects the Domain covers that the caller can open.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

DomainBoardResponse.title: DomainBoardResponse
DomainBoardResponse.description: The Tickets board of a Domain.

own.title: Own
own.description: The contracts the Domain itself provides, by number.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: The contracts of the Domains below it and of the Projects it covers, grouped by provider: Domains first, then Projects, each by name.

builds_against.title: Builds Against
builds_against.description: The contracts the Domain's covered work builds against from outside it.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

key.title: Key
key.description: 3 to 6 uppercase letters or digits, unused in the Account.

parent_ids.title: Parent Ids
parent_ids.description: The Domains to put it in; empty puts it directly under the Account domain. The caller needs domain.manage on each, or on the Account domain.

id.title: Id
id.description: The Domain's id, `DOM-` and 32 hex digits.

key.title: Key
key.description: 3 to 6 uppercase letters or digits, unique among the Account's Domain keys and Project prefixes; the prefix of the keys of the Domain's Epics.

is_account_root.title: Is Account Root
is_account_root.description: Whether this is the Account domain.

archived.title: Archived
archived.description: Whether the Domain is archived; it stays readable.

archived_at.title: Archived At
archived_at.description: When it was archived, or null.

parents.title: Parents
parents.description: The ids of the Domains it is directly in; empty when it sits directly under the Account domain.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: The ids of the Projects directly in it.

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: The ids of the Domains directly in it.

people.description: How many people are granted on it.

epics.description: The Domain Epics its home holds, open and in all; for the Account domain, its Account Epics. A Domain's key is fixed once its home holds work.

version.title: Version
version.description: Moves by one with every change to the Domain.

granted.title: Granted
granted.description: Each person granted directly on the Domain, in grant order; grants on a Domain above it hold here too and are listed there.

DomainDetail.title: DomainDetail
DomainDetail.description: A Domain with the people granted directly on it.

epics.title: Epics
epics.description: The Domain Epics: every open one oldest first, or a page of the finished ones (completed or cancelled) with the most recently finished first.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.description: The work under these Epics the caller can open (their members and every ticket under a member), and the work at the other end of a dependency into or out of it. Each ticket appears once.

running.title: Running
running.description: How many tickets of the Projects the Domain covers and the caller can open are executing now, on the open read; null on the finished read.

DomainEpicBoard.title: DomainEpicBoard
DomainEpicBoard.description: A Domain's Epics, open or finished, with only the work under them.

parent_ticket_id.title: Parent Ticket Id
parent_ticket_id.description: Move the Ticket into an Epic (its id or key), between Epics, or out of its Epic with `null`: a Project Epic of the same Project, or a Domain Epic whose domain covers the Ticket's Project, directly or through a subdomain (else 422 PARENT_PROJECT_MISMATCH or PARENT_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN). Only a Ticket without a parent, a member of an Epic, or an Epic moves, before its execution starts (`backlog`, the planning stages, `implementation_ready`). An Epic's only parent is a Domain Epic (422 EPIC_HAS_NO_PARENT), and a Domain Epic's only a Domain Epic of a domain above its own (422 PARENT_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN); a task has no children (422 TASK_HAS_NO_CHILDREN), and a story gains children through its plan (422 PARENT_NOT_EPIC). A member sorts by its Epic; a Ticket moved out of every Epic goes to the end of its priority in its Project's list.

Eligibility and active-run assignment effects are the admin assign command's, and it needs ticket.update as that command does: the Agent must be an active Agent of the Ticket's Account, and an Agent-only edit is accepted in any stage the assignment is.

change in which stage is stated on the operation; a request is applied whole or
refused whole.

ListMoveChoice.title: ListMoveChoice
ListMoveChoice.description:
Where a person moves a Ticket in its Project's list, or the priority they give it.

For `reposition` (Move): exactly one anchor, `before` or `after`, the Ticket (its id or
key) of the same Project's list that this one lands right before or right after; a move
names an anchor, never a position number, so moves drafted together apply one after
another. Moved across a priority band the Ticket takes the band it lands in; dropped on a
band boundary it keeps its priority. For `reprioritize` (Change priority): `priority`,
P0-P4; a Ticket in the list moves to the nearest edge of its new band. Required for both.
Send the same choice to preview and to execute: its digest covers it, and an execute
with another one is `PREVIEW_STALE`.

The scheduler starts nothing for a Ticket that has a live run (``pending``,
``running``, ``paused`` or ``awaiting_input``). A Ticket at Implementation Ready
that such a run still holds — typically a superseded refinement run parked at a
gate — never starts until that run is terminal. ``runs`` names each run and the
node(s) it waits at; ``message`` names the supported recovery, a run-scoped
terminate of a superseded refinement run. Cleared as soon as no run is live.

PlanAnswer.title: PlanAnswer
PlanAnswer.description:
A person's answer to one decision of a plan.

`decision` is the decision's position in the plan's decisions (`effects.decisions` of
the preview), from 0. Give exactly one of `alternative` (one of that decision's
`alternatives`, verbatim) and `free_text` (the person's own answer). An answer equal to
what the plan already chose is not a correction.

reference_url.description: An optional link to where the brief came from.

PlanContextArtifact.title: PlanContextArtifact
PlanContextArtifact.description:
A brief a child plan attaches to one child, stored as that child's context artifact.

A brief tells the agent that implements the child how to start: the files to change, the
patterns to copy, the contract rows and the narrowest test to iterate with. It reaches the
implementation prompt with the rest of the Ticket.

answers.title: Answers
answers.description: One answer per corrected decision; at least one.

PlanCorrection.title: PlanCorrection
PlanCorrection.description:
What a person answers when they correct a plan's decisions (`correct_plan_decision`).

Send the same correction to preview and to execute: the preview shows the answers it
would record, its digest covers them, and an execute with other answers is
`PREVIEW_STALE`. A preview without it lists the plan's decisions, so a person can choose.

PolicyRefreshPlan.title: PolicyRefreshPlan
PolicyRefreshPlan.description:
What refreshing a run's operational policy would change; nothing is written.

The graph is never changed: `diff` lists only the retry and node policy fields that
move, with each side's provenance. Apply it with
`POST /api/v1/tickets/{ticket_id}/policy-refresh`, sending `plan_digest`,
`expected_policy_digest` and `new_policy_digest` back unchanged. `no_op` is true when
the run's policy is already current.
