PreflightHarness.title: PreflightHarness
PreflightHarness.description:
One coding-agent CLI the node configuration enables.

Attributes:
    harness: The harness (``claude``, ``codex``, ...).
    cli_present: Whether its CLI resolves.
    version: The CLI's version, or ``None`` when absent or illegible.
    login: Its adapter's credential-readiness check; no credential is reported.
    subscriptions: Each subscription the worker holds for it, in preference order, the
        first being the primary. Empty from a worker that reports none, which holds one
        ``unattributed`` subscription, ``default``.
    live_steering: Whether the adapter takes instructions after its run has started,
        sent from protocol minor 9; ``None`` from a node that did not say. Recorded,
        not acted on here: the registry's own capability decides.

PreflightRepository.description:

Attributes:
    project_id: The Project whose remote the App Service named as a probe target.
    reached: Whether ``git ls-remote`` with the machine's own credentials reached it in
        either form.
    form: The form that worked, ``ssh`` or ``https``; ``None`` exactly when neither did.

PreflightSubscription.title: PreflightSubscription
PreflightSubscription.description:
One provider subscription a worker holds for a harness.

Attributes:
    label: The subscription's name in the worker's node configuration.
    fingerprint: A SHA-256 over the provider's own stable account identifier, never a
        token; ``unattributed`` when the worker could not read one. Two workers logged
        into one provider account report one fingerprint and share its limits.
    login: That subscription's credential-readiness check, or ``duplicate`` (from
        protocol minor 2.10) when an earlier subscription of the harness is logged into
        the same provider account and so shares its limit.

PreflightTool.description:

    version: The version it reported, or ``None`` when absent or illegible.
    meets_floor: Whether that version meets the worker's floor for it.

``reason`` is why: the conversation does not fit the model's window, the workspace
snapshot did not verify, the Project has no forge, or the hand-off could not be built.
``subscription_label`` is the subscription the hand-off was refused on, and
``paused_on`` the one the work waits for instead.

ProviderPauseLiftProjection.title: ProviderPauseLiftProjection
ProviderPauseLiftProjection.description:
A person's early resume of a provider pause that the provider refused.

``outcome`` is ``still_exhausted``: the provider had not applied the plan change or the
added credits yet, so the work went back on hold at the provider's newly stated reset.

ProviderPauseWindowProjection.title: ProviderPauseWindowProjection
ProviderPauseWindowProjection.description: One shut provider capacity window of a subscription, and when it reopens.

ProviderRateLimitProjection.title: ProviderRateLimitProjection
ProviderRateLimitProjection.description:

Bounded on purpose: it answers "why is nothing happening, and until when" and nothing
else. ``resets_at`` is the provider's own stated reopening instant, not Pidgen's estimate,
which is what makes it safe to show an operator as a wait rather than as a fault.

ProviderSubscriptionPauseProjection.title: ProviderSubscriptionPauseProjection
ProviderSubscriptionPauseProjection.description:
A provider subscription that could serve the paused work, and its shut windows.

``subscription_label`` names the subscription; it is ``null`` when its worker reported
no label. ``resets_at`` is when the subscription reopens, the latest of its shut windows;
it is ``null`` when the subscription is open.

RefinementStartFailureProjection.title: RefinementStartFailureProjection
RefinementStartFailureProjection.description:
A Refinery start abandoned after its bounded failure retries ran out.

``REFINERY_START_RETRY_EXHAUSTED``: a genuine start error, retried and given up on. A
worker shortage never reaches it; that is a :class:`RefinementStartWaitProjection`.

RefinementStartWaitProjection.title: RefinementStartWaitProjection
RefinementStartWaitProjection.description:
The Ticket's refinement start waits for a worker, from its first refusal.

Worker admission refused the start, so it stays ``applying`` and is retried each
scheduler pass without spending a failure attempt. ``state`` is the
wait's kind and decides what clears it:

- ``waiting_for_worker`` -- no live host could take the start; a live host clears it.
  A wait recorded while a full host still refused a start may carry the
  ``no_headroom`` cause.
  ``constrained_contracts`` names the exhausted capacity (the prompt slots of a
  workflow with prompts, not its first step) and ``hosts`` each host's ready supply
  and the runs charged against it.
- ``no_eligible_worker`` -- no live worker's scope admits the Ticket; an enrolment,
  scope or roster change clears it.
- ``contract_unsupported`` -- every live host lacks a contract or harness the run
  needs; freed capacity cannot clear it, a host that serves it can.

Distinct from :class:`RefinementStartFailureProjection`, a genuine start error whose
retries are exhausted.

TicketKind.title: TicketKind

What a Ticket is in the tree of work.

``EPIC`` is a delivery program: it contains Stories and Tasks and does no work of its own.
``STORY`` is a parent: it contains Stories and Tasks, and its closing turn runs after
theirs. ``TASK`` is a leaf. A Task becomes a Story when a child plan is materialized under
it, before its execution has started, and never changes back. Whether a Ticket is a bug is
its ``workflow_type`` (``bugfix``), not its kind.

team_member_id.description: Assigned Agent, in the Ticket's Account. Unset, creation assigns the Account's reserved Unassigned Agent; a persisted Ticket always has one.

version.title: Version
version.description: Database-owned optimistic-concurrency token for governed Ticket mutations.

ticket_number.title: Ticket Number
ticket_number.description: Numeric part of the id, increments per project.

kind.description: Structural kind: `task` (a leaf), `story` (a parent; a Task becomes one when a child plan is materialized under it, before its execution starts) or `epic` (a delivery program). A bug is a `task` or `story` whose workflow_type is `bugfix`.

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.description: An Epic's target date; null for a Story or Task.

branch_mode.description: Where an Epic's members deliver: `project_base`, `create_new` or `target`. Null for a Story or Task.

feature_branch.title: Feature Branch
feature_branch.description: An Epic's feature branch, fixed when the Epic is created; null for the Project base, and for a Story or Task.

feature_branch_cut_at.title: Feature Branch Cut At
feature_branch_cut_at.description: When an Epic's feature branch was cut on the forge; set means nothing is left to cut. A `target` branch, which already exists, records its creation time.

feature_branch_cut_error.title: Feature Branch Cut Error
feature_branch_cut_error.description: The forge's error from the last failed cut of an Epic's feature branch.

execution_admission_digest.title: Execution Admission Digest
execution_admission_digest.description: Current human promotion digest; only valid on a high-level Ticket.

materialized_plan_digest.title: Materialized Plan Digest
materialized_plan_digest.description: Digest of the root Ticket's current materialized child plan.

approval_mode.description: How this ticket's approval gates resolve. `auto` is the creation default and resolves eligible gates itself; choose `manual` at creation to require human review at every gate.

merge_policy.description: Ticket-level merge policy. `null` inherits the Epic's, then the Project's policy; it only applies while the Project has auto-merging enabled.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Legacy priority, 1 (highest) to 10, kept in step with priority_level: P0 writes 1, P1 2, P2 5, P3 7 and P4 9. Read priority_level instead.

priority_level.description: Priority, 0 to 4 for P0 (most urgent) to P4. Default P2. The Project's list is ordered by priority, then list_position.

list_position.title: List Position
list_position.description: Rank key of a Ticket without a parent in its Project's list: within one priority, keys sort bytewise in list order. Null for a Ticket with a parent.

owner_user_id.title: Owner User Id
owner_user_id.description: Explicit human owner; null inherits the parent's owner or the root's submitter.

prompt_overrides.title: Prompt Overrides
prompt_overrides.description: Complete global-workflow and canonical prompt-node exception set for this Ticket.

prompt_overrides_digest.title: Prompt Overrides Digest
prompt_overrides_digest.description: Canonical digest fencing writes and run-acceptance snapshots.

target_lane.description: Lane this Ticket was asked to occupy once it leaves the Refinery. Persisted from the intent; a `ready_for_implementation` ticket is auto-promoted to IMPLEMENTATION_READY after the Refinery returns it to Backlog, subject to the promotion gate ladder.

auto_promotion_status.description: Outcome of a ready_for_implementation auto-promotion: `pending` while the Refinery runs, then `promoted` or `skipped`. `None` for the default backlog lane.

auto_promotion_reason.title: Auto Promotion Reason
auto_promotion_reason.description: Why a ready_for_implementation auto-promotion was skipped (the failing gate), or empty on success.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: The tags the Ticket carries, by name ignoring case; empty when none.

usage_flags.title: Usage Flags
usage_flags.description: Why this Ticket's work looks wasteful, if it does: a step that ran three times in one pass (`repeated`), or known tokens at least three times the Project's median per completed Ticket once ten Tickets have completed (`expensive`). Empty when nothing is flagged. Flags only explain: they never stop work and set no spending limit.

TicketResource.title: TicketResource
TicketResource.description:
A Ticket of the request's Account with its compact read facts.

The Ticket fields, then what list cards and detail share: the assigned Agent,
lineage, backlog readiness, admission and scheduler readiness, the waits and stops
holding it, and its cohort's progress.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

TicketResponse.title: TicketResponse
TicketResponse.description: One Ticket of the request's Account, with its detail.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the Ticket's latest top-level workflow run started; null before any.

last_activity_at.title: Last Activity At
last_activity_at.description: When that run's session last produced an agent event (a tool call, a message, a plan; coalesced to at most one write every 15 seconds); null before its first.

step.title: Step
step.description: The node id of the step running in the current phase, such as `test-python`; null when none is running.

step_number.title: Step Number
step_number.description: Which step of the current phase the work is on: the phase's finished steps plus one, at most `step_count`; null when the phase has no steps.

step_count.title: Step Count
step_count.description: How many steps the current phase holds; null when it holds none.

step_started_at.title: Step Started At
step_started_at.description: When the running step's latest attempt started; null when no step is running or its attempt records no start.

next_step.title: Next Step
next_step.description: The node id of the step that comes after the running one in the current phase: the first later step that has not finished; null when the running step is the phase's last or none is running.

next_phase.title: Next Phase
next_phase.description: The lifecycle phase after the current one, the first later phase not done; null when the current phase is the last.

TicketRunActivity.title: TicketRunActivity
TicketRunActivity.description:
How a working Ticket's run is going: when it started, when it last did something, and
which step of its current phase it is on.

Read only while the Ticket is executing or planning; every field is null when nothing
records it (no run yet, a session with no agent event, a phase with no steps).

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

TicketRunListResponse.title: TicketRunListResponse
TicketRunListResponse.description: A Ticket's workflow runs, newest first.

seen_at.title: Seen At
seen_at.description: When you last opened the Ticket: the later of the time stored before the call and the one the call named. It never moves backward, so it is not always the time you sent.

TicketSeen.title: TicketSeen
TicketSeen.description: Your seen boundary on a Ticket after the call.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

TicketSeenResponse.title: TicketSeenResponse
TicketSeenResponse.description: The caller's own seen boundary; no other person's is ever readable.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: The session's id, `SES-` and eight characters.

ticket_id.title: Ticket Id
ticket_id.description: The internal id of the Ticket the session works on.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: The agent that runs the session.

agent_role.title: Agent Role
agent_role.description: The role the agent plays in the session.

agent_type.title: Agent Type
agent_type.description: The kind of agent runtime, e.g. `dag`.

status.description: Where the session is in its lifecycle.

current_node.title: Current Node
current_node.description: The workflow node it is running, or null.

current_task.title: Current Task
current_task.description: What it is doing now, or null.

progress_description.title: Progress Description
progress_description.description: A sentence on its progress; may be empty.

last_event_at.title: Last Event At
last_event_at.description: When it last emitted an event, or null.

ended_at.title: Ended At
ended_at.description: When it ended, or null while it is open.

events_emitted.title: Events Emitted
events_emitted.description: How many events the session has emitted.

tokens_used.title: Tokens Used
tokens_used.description: The tokens the session has used so far.

token_usage_complete.title: Token Usage Complete
token_usage_complete.description: Whether every turn of the session reported its usage.

cost_estimate.title: Cost Estimate
cost_estimate.description: The estimated cost of the session so far.

tool_calls_made.title: Tool Calls Made
tool_calls_made.description: How many tool calls the session has made.

errors_encountered.title: Errors Encountered
errors_encountered.description: How many errors the session has met.

human_interventions.title: Human Interventions
human_interventions.description: How many times a person stepped in.

had_errors.title: Had Errors
had_errors.description: Whether the session met any error.

checkpoint_data.title: Checkpoint Data
checkpoint_data.description: The state the session last checkpointed, or null.

prompt_version.title: Prompt Version
prompt_version.description: The version of the prompt configuration it ran with, or null.

loaded_skills.title: Loaded Skills
loaded_skills.description: The skills loaded into the session.

workflow_id.title: Workflow Id
workflow_id.description: The workflow it belongs to, or null.

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id
workspace_id.description: The workspace it runs in, or null.

cwd.title: Cwd
cwd.description: The working directory the workstation reported for the session, or null. It is an opaque value that names a path on the workstation.

last_activity_at.title: Last Activity At
last_activity_at.description: When the session last did something: a tool call or result, a message, reasoning, a checklist update or a file change. Written at most every 15 seconds while the session streams; null before its first activity.

activity_kind.title: Activity Kind
activity_kind.description: What that activity was: `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `message`, `reasoning`, `plan` or `file_changed`; later releases may add kinds. Null before its first activity.

activity_target.title: Activity Target
activity_target.description: What it acted on, at most 200 characters with credentials redacted: a file, pattern or command for a tool call, a path for a file change. Null when the activity names nothing.

TicketSession.title: TicketSession
TicketSession.description: One agent session of a Ticket: a single agent execution, its progress and its usage.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

TicketSessionListResponse.title: TicketSessionListResponse
TicketSessionListResponse.description: A Ticket's agent sessions, newest first, at most 100.

TicketSessionStatus.title: TicketSessionStatus
TicketSessionStatus.description: Where an agent session is in its lifecycle.

TicketStage.title: TicketStage
TicketStage.description: The eleven canonical stages a Ticket can occupy.

stage_label.title: Stage Label
stage_label.description: The lifecycle stage in the board's words.

situation.title: Situation
situation.description: The situation, in the product's words.

sentence.title: Sentence
sentence.description: Why, naming the cause and who or what it waits for.

cause.title: Cause
cause.description: Why the ticket is not moving; null when it is moving. One of `active_ticket_limit`, `epic_share`, `platform_ceiling`, `prompt_capacity_quarantine`, `scheduler_paused`, `fleet_paused`, `worker_capacity` or `dependency`; of the worker and workspace waits, `no_eligible_worker` (every worker that can run it is offline), `no_worker_exists` (the Account has no worker that can run its Agent), `worker_drained` (the only workers that can were drained by their owners), `workstation_offline` (its workspace is on a workstation that is offline), `workspace_residue` (files no run accounts for), `git_admission_blocked`, `stranded_run` (Executing · Recovering: the run stopped reporting), and `agent_preferences_published` (Backlog · Sent back to planning: publishing its Agent's preferences withdrew its readiness). Branch on `code`, not the words; render an unknown cause by its `situation` and `sentence`.

since.title: Since
since.description: When the cause began (ISO 8601), or null when the server does not record it.

addressed_to.title: Addressed To
addressed_to.description: Whose Inbox the wait counts in: the ticket's `owner`, the `worker_owners` of the workers that could run it, or the `account_admins` (the Account's Owners and Administrators, when no worker exists); null when it counts for nobody, as a drained worker does.

details.title: Details
details.description: The cause's facts, such as `{used, limit}`, `{epic_id, epic_name, running, share}`, `{harness, until}`, `{host_id, worker_name, offline_since, auto_move_at}`, `{run_id, host_id, worker_name}`, `{agent_id, agent_name, preferences_version, published_by: {user_id, display_name} or null, published_at}` or, when a worker refused the work because the remote branch does not hold what Pidgen delivered (Stopped · Push refused), `{branch, foreign_commits: [{sha, subject}], refusal}`: the remote branch (null when not recorded), the commits the refusal named with their subject (null when not recorded; empty when none were named) and the refusal code, such as `remote_branch_missing_delivered_commits`; or, for a stopped run (Failed · Recovery available), `{cause}`: why it stopped in one plain sentence, naming the failing criterion or the error and never a code (may be absent from older responses); empty when the sentence says it all.

attention.title: Attention
attention.description: `needs_attention` when a person must act, `in_progress` while work runs, `outcome` otherwise.

also_holding.title: Also Holding
also_holding.description: Every other thing holding the ticket, in order; empty when one thing does.

last_result_at.title: Last Result At
last_result_at.description: When the ticket's work last produced a result (ISO 8601), or null.

phases.title: Phases
phases.description: Exactly five phases, in the order plan, implement, verify, review, deliver.

TicketStatusProjection.title: TicketStatusProjection
TicketStatusProjection.description:
Where the ticket is and what holds it, in one line, with its five phases.

`stage_label` is the lifecycle stage in the board's words and `situation` the
situation in plain language; `code` (`<stage>.<situation>`) is the stable identifier
clients branch on instead of the words. When several things hold the ticket the
situation names the first and `also_holding` lists the rest in order. A situation the
server does not record yet is never produced; new codes are added over time, and a
client renders an unknown code by its words.

submitted_by.description: The person who submitted the Ticket: who submitted the request it was created from, else who created it. Null when no person is recorded.

TicketSubmission.title: TicketSubmission
TicketSubmission.description:
What the submitter asked for, recorded once when the Ticket was created.

Later edits to the Ticket's title or objective never change it.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Their name as people read it now; null when it is not known in the Ticket's Account.

TicketSubmitter.title: TicketSubmitter
TicketSubmitter.description: The person who submitted a Ticket.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Response metadata (pagination and the like), when the route has any.

TicketTagsResponse.title: TicketTagsResponse
TicketTagsResponse.description: The Ticket's tags after the change, by name ignoring case.

root_ticket_id.title: Root Ticket Id
root_ticket_id.description: The root of the Ticket's lineage.

is_root.title: Is Root
is_root.description: Whether the Ticket is the root of its lineage.

descendant_count.title: Descendant Count
descendant_count.description: How many descendants a root has; 0 otherwise.

terminal_outcome.title: Terminal Outcome
terminal_outcome.description: How the Ticket ended, or null while open.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: Its runs in chain order, with attempts.

root_lineage_subtotal.description: Every attempt of the lineage, present only when the Ticket is a root with descendants. It is reported apart from, and never added to, `ticket_subtotal`.

by_model.title: By Model
by_model.description: The Ticket's own turns per harness and model: the four token types and the cost, partial when any of them is unpriced.

root_lineage_by_model.title: Root Lineage By Model
root_lineage_by_model.description: The same roll-up over the whole lineage (the Ticket with its pieces), present only beside `root_lineage_subtotal`.

TicketUsage.title: TicketUsage
TicketUsage.description: One Ticket's runs, node attempts, sessions and token subtotals, read from facts only.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The workflow node.

fan_out_key.title: Fan Out Key
fan_out_key.description: The fan-out item, or an empty string.

logical_attempt.title: Logical Attempt
logical_attempt.description: The attempt number of the node, from 1.

status.title: Status
status.description: How the attempt ended or where it is.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: The session that ran it, or null.

harness.title: Harness
harness.description: The harness that ran it, or null.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When it started: UTC ISO-8601, or null.

ended_at.title: Ended At
ended_at.description: When it ended: UTC ISO-8601, or null.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: Its duration in milliseconds, or null.

queue_duration_ms.title: Queue Duration Ms
queue_duration_ms.description: How long it queued, in milliseconds.

input_tokens.title: Input Tokens
input_tokens.description: Input tokens, or null when not reported.

output_tokens.title: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Output tokens, or null when not reported.

total_tokens.title: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Total tokens, or null when not reported.

token_measurement.title: Token Measurement
token_measurement.description: How the tokens were measured, or null.

token_accounting_version.title: Token Accounting Version
token_accounting_version.description: The token accounting version of the measurement, or null for a legacy one.

usage_complete.title: Usage Complete
usage_complete.description: Whether the attempt reported complete usage.

is_turn.title: Is Turn
is_turn.description: Whether the attempt is an agent turn.

uncached_input_tokens.title: Uncached Input Tokens
uncached_input_tokens.description: Input tokens that were neither read from nor written to the cache: input minus cache read minus cache write. Uncached input, cache write, cache read and output add up to `total_tokens`. Defined only under token accounting version 2 with both cache figures known: null for a legacy (version-null) attempt and for one missing a cache figure, never a clamped zero. Null when the input is not reported.

fresh_input_tokens.title: Fresh Input Tokens
fresh_input_tokens.description: Uncached input plus cache write: the input tokens sent to the model for the first time. Null exactly where `uncached_input_tokens` is.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: Its cost in micros of the display currency (a million is one unit); null when nothing priced it, never zero for an unpriced attempt.

cost_basis.title: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: Which step of the cost order priced it: `reported` (the harness's own figure, or the measured zero of a step that called no model), `account_price` (the Account's price beside the harness option), `list_price` (the price register) or `unavailable` (no price set; `cost_micros` is null).

price_version.title: Price Version
price_version.description: The id of the price it was priced at: the price-register entry for `list_price`, the Account price for `account_price`; null otherwise.

automatic_rework.title: Automatic Rework
automatic_rework.description: True when the attempt belongs to a loop a failed check started inside its run: a verifier or a test join sending the work back to its loop, or a rejected output sending its producer back. A person's Request changes (a new run), a pass a person opened, a retry and a loop iterating on its own are not.

TicketUsageAttempt.title: TicketUsageAttempt
TicketUsageAttempt.description:
One logical node attempt as its analytics fact records it.

`is_turn` marks a dispatched prompt attempt whose delivery started. A null cache figure
means the harness did not report it, never zero; a null `token_accounting_version` is a
legacy measurement.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.description: How many node attempts (turns, by model) it covers.

uncached_input_tokens.title: Uncached Input Tokens
uncached_input_tokens.description: Input tokens that were neither read from nor written to the cache: input minus cache read minus cache write. Uncached input, cache write, cache read and output add up to `total_tokens`. Defined only under token accounting version 2 with both cache figures known: null for a legacy (version-null) attempt and for one missing a cache figure, never a clamped zero.

fresh_input_tokens.title: Fresh Input Tokens
fresh_input_tokens.description: Known fresh input tokens over the turns. Uncached input plus cache write: the input tokens sent to the model for the first time. Null exactly where `uncached_input_tokens` is.

cache_write_tokens.title: Cache Write Tokens
cache_write_tokens.description: Known cache-write tokens over the turns.

cache_read_tokens.title: Cache Read Tokens
cache_read_tokens.description: Known cache-read tokens over the turns.

output_tokens.title: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Known output tokens over the turns.

total_tokens.title: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Known total tokens over the turns.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: The cost of the priced attempts, in micros of the display currency (a million is one unit). An unpriced attempt is left out, never counted as zero; null only when there are attempts and none is priced.

cost_partial.title: Cost Partial
cost_partial.description: True when any attempt in scope is unpriced (`cost_basis` `unavailable`), so `cost_micros` covers only part of it.

TicketUsageCost.title: TicketUsageCost
TicketUsageCost.description:
The four token types and the cost of some node attempts.

Token figures are known-usage sums over the turns among them. Uncached input, cache
write, cache read and output add up to the total. The cost sums the priced attempts and
`cost_partial` says when any is unpriced.

numerator.title: Numerator
numerator.description: How many of the covered kind there are.

ratio.title: Ratio
ratio.description: `numerator / denominator`, null when there are none.

TicketUsageCoverage.title: TicketUsageCoverage
TicketUsageCoverage.description:
A coverage measure, stated as its integers as well as its ratio.

A bare ratio cannot tell 15/16 from 150/160.

metric_schema_version.title: Metric Schema Version
metric_schema_version.description: The version of the metric definitions served.

generated_at.title: Generated At
generated_at.description: When the response was produced: UTC ISO-8601.

data_through.title: Data Through
data_through.description: The time the facts cover up to, or null.

projection_lag_seconds.title: Projection Lag Seconds
projection_lag_seconds.description: How far the facts lag, or null.

TicketUsageMeta.title: TicketUsageMeta
TicketUsageMeta.description: How fresh the projection the figures were read from is.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.description: How many node attempts (turns, by model) it covers.

uncached_input_tokens.title: Uncached Input Tokens
uncached_input_tokens.description: Input tokens that were neither read from nor written to the cache: input minus cache read minus cache write. Uncached input, cache write, cache read and output add up to `total_tokens`. Defined only under token accounting version 2 with both cache figures known: null for a legacy (version-null) attempt and for one missing a cache figure, never a clamped zero.

fresh_input_tokens.title: Fresh Input Tokens
fresh_input_tokens.description: Known fresh input tokens over the turns. Uncached input plus cache write: the input tokens sent to the model for the first time. Null exactly where `uncached_input_tokens` is.

cache_write_tokens.title: Cache Write Tokens
cache_write_tokens.description: Known cache-write tokens over the turns.

cache_read_tokens.title: Cache Read Tokens
cache_read_tokens.description: Known cache-read tokens over the turns.

output_tokens.title: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Known output tokens over the turns.

total_tokens.title: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Known total tokens over the turns.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: The cost of the priced attempts, in micros of the display currency (a million is one unit). An unpriced attempt is left out, never counted as zero; null only when there are attempts and none is priced.

cost_partial.title: Cost Partial
cost_partial.description: True when any attempt in scope is unpriced (`cost_basis` `unavailable`), so `cost_micros` covers only part of it.

TicketUsageModel.title: TicketUsageModel
TicketUsageModel.description:
The four token types and the cost of the turns one harness and model ran.

Only turns count; a turn that named no harness or model is grouped under null.

meta.description: The freshness of the projection the figures were read from.

TicketUsageResponse.title: TicketUsageResponse
TicketUsageResponse.description: One Ticket's runs, node attempts, sessions and token subtotals.

parent_run_id.title: Parent Run Id
parent_run_id.description: The run it is nested in, or null.

chain_index.title: Chain Index
chain_index.description: Its position in the Ticket's run chain, or null.

chain_role.title: Chain Role
chain_role.description: Its role in the chain, or null.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: The session it ran in, or null.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: Its earliest attempt start: UTC ISO-8601.

ended_at.title: Ended At
ended_at.description: Its latest attempt end: UTC ISO-8601.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.description: Its node attempts, in start order.

TicketUsageRun.title: TicketUsageRun
TicketUsageRun.description:
One run of the Ticket, in run-chain order.

A nested run has no chain index and follows the run that contains it.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: The session, or null for attempts with none.

run_ids.title: Run Ids
run_ids.description: The runs the session took part in, in chain order.

TicketUsageSession.title: TicketUsageSession
TicketUsageSession.description:
The Ticket's attempts grouped by session.

Attempts with no session are grouped under a null `session_id`, so the session subtotals
add up to the Ticket's subtotal.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.description: How many node attempts the roll-up covers.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: How many runs they belong to.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.description: How many Tickets they belong to.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: How many of them are agent turns.

input_tokens.title: Input Tokens
input_tokens.description: Known input tokens over the turns.

output_tokens.title: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Known output tokens over the turns.

cache_read_tokens.title: Cache Read Tokens
cache_read_tokens.description: Known cache-read tokens over the turns.

cache_write_tokens.title: Cache Write Tokens
cache_write_tokens.description: Known cache-write tokens over the turns.

total_tokens.title: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Known total tokens over the turns.

token_coverage.description: Turns that reported complete usage, out of all turns.

split_coverage.description: Turns that reported an input and output split, out of all turns.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: True when every turn reported complete usage.

uncached_input_tokens.title: Uncached Input Tokens
uncached_input_tokens.description: Known uncached input tokens over the turns. Input tokens that were neither read from nor written to the cache: input minus cache read minus cache write. Uncached input, cache write, cache read and output add up to `total_tokens`. Defined only under token accounting version 2 with both cache figures known: null for a legacy (version-null) attempt and for one missing a cache figure, never a clamped zero.

fresh_input_tokens.title: Fresh Input Tokens
fresh_input_tokens.description: Known fresh input tokens over the turns. Uncached input plus cache write: the input tokens sent to the model for the first time. Null exactly where `uncached_input_tokens` is.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: The cost of the priced attempts, in micros of the display currency (a million is one unit). An unpriced attempt is left out, never counted as zero; null only when there are attempts and none is priced.

cost_partial.title: Cost Partial
cost_partial.description: True when any attempt in scope is unpriced (`cost_basis` `unavailable`), so `cost_micros` covers only part of it.

automatic_rework.description: The tokens and cost of the attempts in scope that are automatic rework: the loops a failed check started inside their run (`automatic_rework` on the attempts). Zero attempts when there were none.

tool_calls.title: Tool Calls
tool_calls.description: Tool calls summed from the sessions' own counts: a session's, the Ticket's sessions' or, on the lineage subtotal, the sessions of the Ticket and its pieces. Null on a run, since one session can span runs, and on attempts with no session.

failed_tool_calls.title: Failed Tool Calls
failed_tool_calls.description: The failed tool calls of the same sessions, from the errors each recorded; null where `tool_calls` is.

TicketUsageSubtotal.title: TicketUsageSubtotal
TicketUsageSubtotal.description:
One roll-up of node attempts.

Token figures are known-usage sums over turns: null only when turns exist and none
reported the figure. `token_coverage` is complete turns over turns and `split_coverage`
is turns that reported an input and output split over turns; `complete` is true exactly
when every turn reported complete usage. An attempt that is not a turn is a measured
zero: counted in `attempts`, never a coverage gap.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the Ticket was created: UTC ISO-8601.

ended_at.title: Ended At
ended_at.description: When it first completed: UTC ISO-8601, or null.

elapsed_ms.title: Elapsed Ms
elapsed_ms.description: The window in milliseconds, or null.

TicketUsageWallTime.title: TicketUsageWallTime
TicketUsageWallTime.description:
The Ticket's elapsed window, from creation to first completion.

`elapsed_ms` is null while the Ticket is open. `attempt_duration_sum_ms` is the sum of
node-attempt durations, published beside it so it is never mistaken for wall time: under
parallel work it exceeds the elapsed window.

message.title: Message
message.description: A sentence for a person; not a stable interface.

TicketUsageWarning.title: TicketUsageWarning
TicketUsageWarning.description:
A disclosure the response attaches to itself.

A stale projection carries `projection_lag_seconds` (integer) and a read that accepted
stale data carries `allow_stale: true`; either appears only when it applies.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Project the workspace belongs to

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: git branch name backing this workspace

base_sha.title: Base Sha
base_sha.description: Immutable commit selected as the workspace creation baseline

head_sha.title: Head Sha
head_sha.description: Exact worktree HEAD last reported by the owning workstation

merge_ref.title: Merge Ref
merge_ref.description: Local merge-back commit sha, recorded when delivery.mode=local.

delivery_mode.title: Delivery Mode
delivery_mode.description: Effective delivery mode materialized at delivery time: local|remote.

locality_domain.title: Locality Domain
locality_domain.description: The workstation whose filesystem holds this worktree. The control plane can neither read nor mutate the path, so this is what routes a maintenance request to the one host that can, and what qualifies `path` into an honest `host:path` label. None means unpinned — provisioned before locality was recorded, or a single-workstation deployment where any workspace worker will do.

retain_branch.title: Retain Branch
retain_branch.description: Teardown must not delete this branch. Cancelling stops work; it does not destroy it, so committed work survives unless the operator explicitly asked for it to be discarded.

cleanup_state.description: Teardown progress. `unreachable` preserves the row and its lifecycle status until the owning workstation or an operator can act.

cleanup_error.title: Cleanup Error
cleanup_error.description: Latest cleanup reachability/failure detail, cleared by a successful request.

deleted_at.title: Deleted At
deleted_at.description: Teardown retires the worktree, not the record. The delivery facts that reference this workspace outlive the files on disk, so the row is stamped rather than removed. This is not a status: an abandoned workspace whose worktree still exists is a live state, and a deleted one may still be `active`.

delivery.description: The Project's effective delivery mode, or null when it could not be resolved.

TicketWorkspace.title: TicketWorkspace
TicketWorkspace.description: The git workspace the Ticket's work happens in: its own, or its parent's.

criterion_index.title: Criterion Index
criterion_index.description: The criterion's position in the Ticket's acceptance_criteria, from 0.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Always MUST: only MUST criteria block.

status.title: Status
status.description: failing, or pending: never verified, or unverifiable.

unverifiable.title: Unverifiable
unverifiable.description: True when the verifier looked and could not prove it.

verifier_note.title: Verifier Note
verifier_note.description: What the verifier said about it, when it said something.

UnprovenCriterion.title: UnprovenCriterion
UnprovenCriterion.description: A MUST acceptance criterion not passing for the revision a delivery review reviews.

fallback_user_ids.title: Fallback User Ids
fallback_user_ids.description: The fallback people, as user ids. Each must be an active Contributor or Manager of the Project. An empty list sends decisions on to the Project's Managers.

independent_approval.title: Independent Approval
independent_approval.description: Whether delivery needs an independent approver. Stored with the settings.

expected_updated_at.title: Expected Updated At
expected_updated_at.description: The updated_at of the settings you read, or null if it was null. A different value means someone saved since, and the write is refused.

UpdateResponsibilityRequest.title: UpdateResponsibilityRequest
UpdateResponsibilityRequest.description: The Project's responsibility settings, replaced whole.

url.title: Url
url.description: A new URL, under the rules of create.

events.title: Events
events.description: A new set of events; at least one.

description.title: Description
description.description: A new description; null clears it.

state.title: State
state.description: `disabled` keeps the endpoint but sends it nothing new.

UpdateWebhookRequest.title: UpdateWebhookRequest
UpdateWebhookRequest.description: What to change; a field left out is left as it is.

kind.description: `repeated` or `expensive`. Branch on this, never on the sentence.

sentence.title: Sentence
sentence.description: What the flag found, in a sentence a person can read.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The step that ran three or more times in one pass (`repeated`), else null.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.description: The most times that step ran in one pass (`repeated`), else null.

ratio.title: Ratio
ratio.description: The Ticket's known tokens as a multiple of the Project's median known tokens per completed Ticket, to one decimal (`expensive`), else null.

UsageFlag.title: UsageFlag
UsageFlag.description:
A note that a Ticket's work looks wasteful: a step ran three times in one pass, or its
known tokens are three times the Project's median per ticket.

A flag only explains. It never stops work and sets no spending limit. A rework pass is not
counted as repeated work.

UsageFlagKind.title: UsageFlagKind
UsageFlagKind.description: What a usage flag says about a Ticket's work.

refusal.description: Why it is not allowed; null when allowed.

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description: Whether something is allowed, with the typed reason when it is not.

WaitingHostProjection.title: WaitingHostProjection
WaitingHostProjection.description:
One candidate host of a waiting refinement start and what holds it.

``ready_supply`` is the host's ready physical slots per capacity contract the run
needs; ``charged_runs`` the pinned runs admission charged against them (at most 20,
``charged_run_count`` counts every one); ``reserved_by_other_work`` slots a run not
pinned here reserves. ``lacking`` names the contracts or ``harness:<adapter>`` a host
refused for what it serves lacks.

ticket_key.description: The Ticket's public key, e.g. NS-166.

category.description: How the person is told: a decision, a review, work that cannot continue.

WorkerAdmissionBlockProjection.title: WorkerAdmissionBlockProjection
WorkerAdmissionBlockProjection.description:
No worker may run this Ticket, so admission refused it.

No live, enabled worker's scope admits the Ticket: none is enrolled for the Account,
each is paused, offline or scoped to other people's or Projects' work, or cannot reach
the Project's repository. The scheduler retries it as soon as one may (a worker
enrolled, widened, resumed or back online), and clears this when it admits it.
